title: Fertilizer Runoff
threat_story: Nutrients from lawns may wash into a pond and contribute to algae growth and oxygen problems.
solution_piece: Native buffer strip between lawn and pond
physical_instruction: Remove fertilizer marker; attach native buffer strip between lawn and pond.

choices.text: Reduce unnecessary fertilizer and protect a vegetated buffer

science_explanation: Vegetated buffers may slow runoff and retain some sediment and nutrients.
real_life_verification: Compare nutrient tests and runoff observations over time; do not infer nutrients from water cloudiness.
demonstration_note: Physical change demonstrates a conservation plan, not a guaranteed ecosystem recovery.

title: Invasive Plants
threat_story: A suspected invasive wetland plant may outcompete native plants.
solution_piece: Native plant piece labeled 'planned after verification'
physical_instruction: Remove suspected-invasive marker; add native plant piece labeled “planned after verification”.

prediction.prompt: What can some invasive plants do?

choices.text: Verify identification and follow approved management, then restore natives

science_explanation: Appropriate management can reduce pressure on native plants, but identification and permissions matter.
real_life_verification: Document plant identification and repeat vegetation surveys.
demonstration_note: Physical change demonstrates a conservation plan, not a guaranteed ecosystem recovery.

title: Pollinator Habitat Decline
threat_story: Few suitable native flowers are present near the pond.
solution_piece: Flowering plant patch with bee/butterfly illustration tokens
physical_instruction: Attach flowering plant patch and bee/butterfly illustration tokens.

prediction.prompt: What resource can native flowers provide?

choices.text: Add locally appropriate native flowers and nesting habitat

science_explanation: Appropriate native flowers can provide nectar and pollen; nesting habitat also matters.
real_life_verification: Observe pollinator visits at comparable times and weather.
demonstration_note: Physical change demonstrates a conservation plan, not a guaranteed ecosystem recovery.

title: Pond Litter
threat_story: Plastic litter is visible along the shoreline.
solution_piece: Covered waste bin and prevention education sign
physical_instruction: Remove plastic litter tokens; attach waste bin and prevention sign.

choices.text: It may cause ingestion or entanglement
Safely remove litter and prevent new litter

science_explanation: Removing litter reduces exposure to harmful debris.
real_life_verification: Count litter items before/after cleanup; use safe supervised procedures.
demonstration_note: Physical change demonstrates a conservation plan, not a guaranteed ecosystem recovery.

title: Shoreline Habitat Loss
threat_story: Vegetation was removed from part of the shoreline.
solution_piece: Planted shore panel with frog shelter illustration
physical_instruction: Swap bare-shore panel for planted shore; add frog shelter illustration.

choices.text: Restore suitable native grasses, sedges, and shrubs

science_explanation: Native vegetation may stabilize soil and create shelter; wildlife presence must be observed, not assumed.
real_life_verification: Compare erosion signs and repeat wildlife observations.
demonstration_note: Physical change demonstrates a conservation plan, not a guaranteed ecosystem recovery.

title: Sediment Runoff
threat_story: Bare soil on a slope washes into the pond during rain.
physical_instruction: Replace exposed slope patch with planted/stabilized slope piece.

choices.text: Reduce light and cover some habitats
Stabilize bare soil and manage runoff
Channel muddy water straight into pond

science_explanation: Stabilized soil may reduce erosion and suspended sediment entering water.
real_life_verification: Compare equal-volume runoff from two model slopes; repeat tests.
demonstration_note: Physical change demonstrates a conservation plan, not a guaranteed ecosystem recovery.
